samples.summary: Gate 1b's refusal surface omits modules that `scripts/verify-self.mjs` imports at module scope, so a branch can neutralize CI and still be auto-promoted with a hand-off comment asserting "the CI definition that run executed came from main"
samples.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (checks.mjs:123-135) covers `scripts/verify-*.mjs` and `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, but `scripts/verify-self.mjs:2-3` imports two further modules at module scope that the list does not match:

  import { extractFailureSummary } from "./failure-summary.mjs";   // scripts/failure-summary.mjs
  import { readHeadSha } from "./agent/git-env.mjs";               // scripts/agent/git-env.mjs

`definesCi("scripts/failure-summary.mjs")` and `definesCi("scripts/agent/git-env.mjs")` both return false (neither starts with `verify-`; `scripts/agent/**` is not on the list at all).

Attack: an `agent:managed` PR (or the agent App itself — both paths are explicitly named as unrestricted in mark-ready.mjs:29-32) adds a top-level side effect to `scripts/failure-summary.mjs`, e.g. `process.exit(0)` or a `process.on('exit')` override. ESM evaluates it before `verify-self.mjs`'s body runs, so `pnpm verify:self` (ci.yml:308) exits 0 having executed zero lanes and the CI run concludes `success`. Then:
  * gate 1 (`ciPassed`, mark-ready.mjs:159) reads that genuinely green run at the genuine path — passes;
  * gate 1b (`ranBaseCiDefinition`, mark-ready.mjs:224) enumerates `pulls/N/files`, finds only `scripts/failure-summary.mjs`, `definesCi` says false — passes;
  * mark-ready.mjs:382-389 then posts a hand-off comment telling the accountable human signer that "the CI definition that run executed came from `main` rather than from the branch", which is false.

Same class, also unmatched by the list: `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/design-sandbox/vitest.config.ts` (ci.yml:318/322 run `vitest` per package, and the config chooses which files are collected — `include: []` yields a green lane with no tests); `scripts/agent/package.json` / lockfile (the `agent:tests` lane); a newly added root `.npmrc` or `.pnpmfile.cjs` (read by `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, ci.yml:300). The comment at checks.mjs:116-121 scopes the residue to "a branch can always edit its own test files", which does not cover disabling the runner or the lane driver.

The mirror test in checks.test.mjs only asserts `CI_DEFINING_PATHS ⊇ harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`; `ciConfig` was written for a different purpose (forcing a full run) and never claimed to enumerate everything `verify:self` executes, so the drift test cannot catch this.
searchedFor: Read pnpm-workspace.yaml (packages/* — one level, so packages/*/package.json is complete)

samples.summary: `capture-collect.yml` is the same forgery class the change hardens elsewhere and got no `path` clause: it consumes `workflow_run` by display name with no path / branch / head-repository guard while holding a cross-repo write PAT
samples.evidence:
This change adds `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to agent-review-panel.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and ci-report.yml, and checks.test.mjs's new "every workflow_run consumer" test enumerates exactly those three. capture-collect.yml consumes the same event class and is left open:

  line 67-69: `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` — display names, which the diff's own reasoning establishes are only a `name:` key and are not unique.
  line 129: `if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped' }}` — the only gate. No `path`, no `head_branch`, no `head_repository.full_name == github.repository`.
  line 142-146: `actions/checkout` of `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `token: ${{ secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN }}` (documented at line 20-23 as a fine-grained PAT with `Contents: read and write` on that repo).
  line 220-259: `git commit` + `git push` with those persisted credentials.

So anyone able to land a workflow file on a branch named `name: Agent Review Panel` can drive a job that pushes to a second repository using a PAT this repository's read-only `permissions:` block otherwise deliberately withholds. It also lets a forged run repeatedly occupy the `capture-collect` concurrency group (line 109-111, `cancel-in-progress: false`), queueing out real collections. The docs added in this change (docs/design/harness-engineering.md, docs/tasks/active/20260825-…-todo.md item 1) acknowledge the gap and defer it to a maintainer, so this is a known-and-recorded exposure rather than an oversight — but the guard is still absent and the new test that would have pinned it is written to take a (file, job) pair and simply does not list this file.
searchedFor: Read the new checks.test.mjs 'every workflow_run consumer' test's (file, job) list
Grep 'workflow_run' consumers: agent-review-panel.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml, ci-report.yml, capture-collect.yml, docker-publish.yml, publish-ghpage.yml

samples.summary: The fixer arm this change hardens still mints a full-installation App token from a mutable `@v1` tag and hands it to a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code
samples.evidence:
agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-115:

  - name: Generate GitHub App token
    id: app-token
    uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1        # mutable tag, handles AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
                                                    # <- no permission-* inputs at all
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
      token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

Two defects in one step. (a) Unpinned: every other consumer in this repo pins `@d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 # v1.12.0` and says why (agent-review-panel.yml:1485-1488 "Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key"). A compromised or retagged `v1` sees `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, i.e. the whole installation, not one token. (b) Unscoped: with no `permission-*` inputs the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — compare agent-fix.yml:121-129 and agent-review-panel.yml:1800-1808, which scope theirs precisely because "this token is live in a job that later checks out and executes untrusted branch code", which is exactly what happens on the next line here (the fixer agent installs, builds and tests the PR branch).

This is directly coupled to the change under review: the diff's justification for the new `path` clause is that a forged `name: CI` run "would otherwise drive this workflow's `contents: write` fixer". Closing the trigger while the token stays full-installation and mutable-tagged leaves the larger half of that arm's blast radius intact. Same pattern at agent-implement.yml:119 and agent-review-reply.yml:126. Recorded as maintainer work in docs/tasks/active/20260825-…-todo.md item 2, but still present in the tree.
searchedFor: Grep 'create-github-app-token' with 8 lines of context across .github/workflows
Compared against agent-fix.yml:121-129 and agent-review-panel.yml:1488-1493 / 1800-1808 (pinned + permission-scoped)

samples.summary: Gate 1b pins the head across its own two reads but nothing re-checks it before the flip and the hand-off comment, so the comment can assert "green for this exact head SHA" about a commit that is no longer the head
samples.evidence:
The diff adds a head re-read inside `ranBaseCiDefinition` (mark-ready.mjs:246-252) precisely because "CI's verdict and the changed-file list are no longer about the same commit" if the head moves. The same reasoning applies to the mutation, and there is no equivalent check: after gate 1b returns, `reviewChecks(pr.headRefOid)` (line 290) and `disclosesAiAuthorship` run, then `ghMutate(["pr", "ready", prNumber])` at line 338 and the hand-off comment at line 401 are issued with no re-read and no expected-head assertion (the REST/GraphQL ready-for-review mutation takes no expectedHeadOid, so it cannot be made atomic — a final `headRefOid` comparison immediately before line 338 is the available mitigation).

A push landing in that window leaves the PR flipped to "ready for human review", labelled `agent:ready`, with a comment (lines 382-389) that states CI is green "for this exact head SHA, on a PR based on the default branch — and the branch changes none of the paths that define what CI does". All three clauses then describe the superseded commit, not the one the human reviewer will read. Impact is bounded (the window is short, merge is still human, and a later CI run on the new head is unrelated to the already-flipped draft state), so this is a stale-attestation weakness rather than an exploit — but it is the same TOCTOU the new head re-read was added to close, one step further down.
searchedFor: Read scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs end to end, tracing the order of ciGate / ciDefinitionGate / reviewChecks / ghMutate
Checked the new gate-1b head re-read at lines 241-252 for whether it covers the mutation
Read the hand-off comment text at lines 375-396 for the property it claims
Read .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml promote job (1453-1550) for any surrounding head pin

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 mints an App token via actions/create-github-app-token@v1 (a mutable tag) while handling secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, and supplies no permission-* inputs, so the token inherits the App installation's full permission set. Lines 111-115 immediately check out the untrusted head branch with that token and without persist-credentials:false, leaving it in .git/config in the workspace. Branch-controlled code then executes in the same job: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at line 285 runs branch lifecycle scripts, and the fixer step (lines 368-430) runs with Bash allowed and receives the same token at line 375. The workflow's own comment at line 119 calls the branch copy 'attacker-influenceable code', so the repo's own threat model treats it as untrusted. The repo convention contradicts this step: agent-fix.yml:119-130 and agent-review-panel.yml:1797-1810 SHA-pin the action (d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 # v1.12.0) and scope permission-contents/pull-requests/issues, explicitly because 'this token is live in a job that later checks out and executes untrusted branch code'. The existing gates (path/fork/managed at lines 52-56 and 91) constrain when the job fires, not the token's provenance or scope, so nothing makes this unreachable. This is secrets exposure plus an over-privileged credential adjacent to untrusted code execution, squarely in the security lane.

finding.summary: Gate 2 ("review panel approved") still identifies lens checks by NAME only — no `app.slug` producer check — which is the exact forgery class this diff closes for gate 1
finding.evidence: This change rewrites mark-ready.mjs's header to explain that identity-by-display-name is forgeable, converts gate 1 to server-side workflow scoping, and in the same breath re-asserts gate 2: "Only the reviewer workflow (which has checks:write) can post that check, so the author agent cannot forge its own approval" (mark-ready.mjs:30-33). But gate 2's implementation is `allRequiredPassed` → `checkPassed` (checks.mjs:159-164), which does `(checkRuns||[]).filter(r => r.name === name)` and reads `conclusion` — it never inspects `r.app`. A check-run name is not a secret and any integration with checks:write may create one. The repo's own code says so in six other places: fix-eligible.mjs:44-48 ("`app.slug === 'github-actions'` is checked because the NAME is not a secret: any integration may create a check run called `agent-review-security`, and without the producer check a third-party app could manufacture a verdict … out of nothing"), rounds.mjs:200/230/585, review-state.mjs:144, loop-status.mjs:193, review-round-guard.mjs:222. Only `checkPassed` — the one used by the PROMOTION gate — omits it. Attack: any actor able to POST a check run to the head SHA (a third-party App installed with Checks:write, or the agent App itself if its installation carries Checks:write — agent-implement.yml:117-122 mints an UNSCOPED installation token and hands it to the model-driven job) creates `agent-review-correctness` / `agent-review-security` with `conclusion: success` on the PR head, and gate 2 reads green with no reviewer having run. set-state.mjs:240 has the same omission (advisory only). Fix is one line, and every other reader already has it.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `checkPassed` identifies lens checks by name only and "never inspects `r.app`". The actual code at scripts/agent/checks.mjs:265-272 filters `r?.name === name && r?.app?.slug === CHECK_PRODUCER_APP_SLUG`, with the constant defined at checks.mjs:257 and documented at checks.mjs:236-256 describing this exact forgery class ("gate 2 was the one reader that did not" — past tense; it now does). The producer filter is applied before the started_at sort, defeating the newer-forged-run shadowing variant. Tests pin it: checks.test.mjs:57 ("a check run from ANOTHER App is not evidence"), :69 (newer forged run does not shadow), :80-81 (missing/empty app → false), :83 (allRequiredPassed propagates). allRequiredPassed (checks.mjs:275-278) delegates per name to checkPassed, so the promotion gate reached from mark-ready.mjs:287 inherits the producer check, and the described attack (third-party App or unscoped installation token posting agent-review-* success on the head SHA) is rejected because app.slug is set by GitHub, not the payload. The only accurate sub-claim is set-state.mjs:240, which the finding itself marks advisory-only; it feeds label reconciliation, not promotion, so it does not sustain the critical claim.

mergedFrom.summary: New gate 1b claims "CI ran main's definition" but its prefix list covers only `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/actions/**` — CI's actual behaviour is defined by branch files the agent App CAN push

finding.summary: Gate 1b's `CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES` is far narrower than the CI-defining surface it claims to cover — a branch can gut CI via `package.json` / `scripts/verify-*.mjs` / `harness.config.json` and still auto-promote, while the new hand-off comment tells the human reviewer the run executed main's CI definition.
finding.evidence: Gate 1b refuses promotion only when a changed path starts with `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` (mark-ready.mjs:175, 189). But `ci.yml` contains almost no test logic: `verify-self` runs `pnpm verify:self` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:308) and `verify-integration` runs `pnpm verify:integration` (ci.yml:752), both resolved from the MERGE REF's `package.json` ("verify:self": "node ./scripts/verify-self.mjs", package.json:25) and executed from the branch's `scripts/verify-self.mjs`. The `changes` job likewise runs the branch's `node ./scripts/changed-areas.mjs` (ci.yml:149) and its `heavy` output gates every step of `verify-browser` / `verify-integration` / coverage (ci.yml:317-321, 484-487, 593-596). ATTACK: under gate 1b's own stated threat model ("an `agent:managed` human PR is on this promote path and is not restricted", mark-ready.mjs:28), the author pushes a commit that changes only `scripts/verify-self.mjs` (or the `verify:self` script in `package.json`, or `harness.config.json` so `heavy=false`) so the lanes no-op. `.github/workflows/**` is untouched, so `branchEditsCiDefinition` returns false, gate 1b passes, gate 1 sees a genuinely green run of the genuine `ci.yml`, and the PR is auto-promoted. The repo already knows the real surface: `harness.config.json`'s `ciConfig` list (harness.config.json:52-62) names `harness.config.json`, `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, `scripts/verify-*.mjs`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `knip.json` alongside `.github/workflows/**` — gate 1b uses none of them, and `ciConfig` only forces a full run rather than refusing promotion. The harm is amplified rather than mitigated by this delta: the hand-off comment now asserts "the branch changes no workflow definition, so that run executed the CI file on `main` rather than one the branch supplied" (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) and the design doc's honest "WHAT THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE" paragraph was replaced with "Gate 1b closes that" (mark-ready.mjs:19) — a gate that reads as covered to

verdict.reason: The finding describes a narrower earlier revision of gate 1b that is not in this tree. There is no `CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES` and no `branchEditsCiDefinition` anywhere in the repo; gate 1b calls `definesCi()` (mark-ready.mjs:71, 205), whose surface `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (checks.mjs:123-135) explicitly includes every path the claimed attack depends on: `scripts/verify-*.mjs`, root `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `harness.config.json`, `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, `knip.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, plus `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/actions/**`. A branch that changes only `scripts/verify-self.mjs`, the `verify:self` script in `package.json`, or `harness.config.json` therefore produces `hits.length > 0` and gate 1b returns false (mark-ready.mjs:254-260), refusing promotion. The mirror against `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig` (harness.config.json:52-62) is machine-enforced by checks.test.mjs:492-512, and checks.test.mjs:516-532 asserts `definesCi` is true for exactly those attack paths. The claimed hand-off text is also not present: mark-ready.mjs:382-389 names the full `ci.ciConfig` surface and keeps the "does NOT mean every assertion CI ran is main's" caveat, and the "WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT COVER" paragraph the finding says was removed is at checks.mjs:116-121. checks.mjs:89-96 documents the finding's exact hole as the fixed prior revision.

mergedFrom.summary: Gate 1b reads the LIVE PR file list, not the diff at the SHA gate 1 verified — a push between the two reads bypasses it

finding.summary: Gate 1b's evidence (`pulls/{n}/files`) is diffed against the PR's BASE ref, which the PR author can change at will and which is not pinned to the SHA gate 1 read — retargeting the base after CI starts empties the file list and lets a workflow-editing branch through.
finding.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` asks `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files` (mark-ready.mjs:183), which returns the base..head diff for the PR's CURRENT base branch — a mutable, author-controlled field — whereas gate 1's evidence is a CI run pinned to `pr.headRefOid` (mark-ready.mjs:158, 166). ATTACK (same threat model as the gate: a collaborator opening an `agent:managed` PR): (1) push branch `x` containing a gutted `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; (2) open the PR from that head against `main`, so CI's `pull_request: branches: ["main"]` trigger (ci.yml:9-10) fires and runs the branch's gutted `ci.yml` on the merge ref, concluding green; the panel starts on `workflow_run: requested` and `promote` waits for the conclusion (agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1462); (3) before the promote job runs `mark-ready`, retarget the PR's base to another branch in the same repo that already carries the same gutted `ci.yml`. Retargeting neither cancels the already-created CI run nor changes `headRefOid`, so gate 1 still reads `success` — but `pulls/{n}/files` now diffs against the new base and reports no `.github/workflows/**` entry, so gate 1b passes and the PR is promoted with the hand-off comment claiming main's CI definition ran. A slower variant needs no race: retarget after the refusal, then `@claude rerun`, whose `workflow_run: completed` with `run_attempt > 1` is explicitly admitted by the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169). I could not execute this to confirm GitHub does not cancel the in-flight run on retarget, hence medium confidence. A base-independent check (e.g. comparing the head tree's `.github/workflows/**` against the default branch, or reading the run's own `head_sha` tree) would not have this property.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts gate 1b diffs against the PR's mutable base with no pin, citing a function `branchEditsCiDefinition` at mark-ready.mjs:183. Neither the function nor the unpinned behaviour exists. The gate-1b entry point is `ranBaseCiDefinition` (mark-ready.mjs:224), and BEFORE it fetches `pulls/{n}/files` (mark-ready.mjs:199) it reads the repository's `default_branch` via `defaultBranch()` (mark-ready.mjs:216-222) and throws unless `pr.baseRefName` equals it (mark-ready.mjs:231-237). That throw is caught at mark-ready.mjs:262-269, returns false, and mark-ready.mjs:315-318 exits 1 without promoting. Both narrated attacks are therefore blocked: retargeting the base onto a sibling branch that already carries a gutted ci.yml makes `baseRefName != default_branch`, and the slower `@claude rerun` variant re-runs the whole script, which re-reads `baseRefName` fresh at mark-ready.mjs:137-143. The head is separately re-pinned after enumeration (mark-ready.mjs:246-252), and `defaultBranch()` fails closed when `default_branch` is unreadable. The behaviour is pinned by tests at scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:404-448 (retargeted base -> exit 1 with "not the default branch 'main'"; renamed default branch honoured; missing default_branch fails closed). The only residual is a sub-second TOCTOU between the `pr view` at line 137 and the files fetch at line 199 — a different mechanism, requiring a race inside one job step, and explicitly excluded by the finding's own "needs no race" claim.

searchedFor: read capture-collect.yml trigger, if:, permissions and store checkout
grep artifact selection and meta validation in collect-captures.mjs
finding.summary: The change enumerates every display-name-triggered `workflow_run` consumer and omits capture-collect.yml, which is triggered by display name and holds a cross-repo push secret
finding.evidence: The rationale added in three places (agent-iterate-ci.yml:44-51, agent-review-panel.yml:156-163, ci-report.yml:47-53) and the design doc claim the set is complete: the three agent workflows assert `path`, and "docker-publish.yml / publish-ghpage.yml need no clause — their `head_branch == 'main'` gate means a forgery would have to be merged first". capture-collect.yml is not mentioned. It triggers on `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` (capture-collect.yml:67-69) — display names again — with the only gate being `conclusion != 'skipped'` (capture-collect.yml:129): no `path`, no `head_repository`, no `head_branch`. Any run named "Agent Review Panel" invokes it, including a run produced by a `pull_request` workflow file added in a FORK's PR, which executes in the base repo and emits `workflow_run`. The invoked job checks out `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN` (capture-collect.yml:142-146) and pushes to it. It runs main's collector, so this is not RCE; the reachable impact is unauthorised invocation of a secret-bearing cross-repo writer, plus collection of artifacts an outside contributor's run uploaded under the capture name prefix (collect-captures.mjs:437-450 matches on artifact name prefix; parseMeta only shape-checks `workflow`/`event`, collect-captures.mjs:234-237). If the path clause is the right answer for ci-report, the same reasoning applies here.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. capture-collect.yml triggers on workflow_run matched by DISPLAY NAME (67-69) and the job's sole gate is conclusion != 'skipped' (129) — no path, no head_repository, no head_branch, no environment: protection — while that job checks out dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval with secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN (142-146, creds persisted) and pushes (258). Every sibling workflow_run consumer does carry such a clause (agent-review-panel.yml:166-167, agent-iterate-ci.yml:54-56, ci-report.yml:55-56, docker-publish.yml:68-71, publish-ghpage.yml:43-46), so none of them is a counterexample for this file. I also looked for an indirect guard downstream: the collector selects artifacts by NAME PREFIX only (collect-captures.mjs:105 and planCollection 436-459) and parseMeta only shape-checks fields (196-242), so nothing ties a collected artifact to a trusted producer workflow, branch or repository. One reviewer sub-claim is wrong and does not rescue the finding: the design doc DOES mention this file — harness-engineering.md:2045-2059 states it is 'the same class and is NOT yet guarded — an open gap' and names the missing github.event.workflow_run.path clause as the fix — which corroborates rather than refutes the absence. collect-captures.test.mjs:1320-1323 pins the if: to exactly the conclusion-only expression, so the unguarded form is asserted, not accidental. Impact is bounded (read-only permissions block 101-103, token scoped to one other public repo, and collect-captures.test.mjs:1248-1273 pins that no untrusted ref is ever checked out), which matches 'major' rather than 'critical', but a display-name-forgeable trigger reaching a cross-repo write credential is a missing authorization gate squarely in the security lane. No counterexample found.

searchedFor: grep 'git apply' across scripts to confirm nothing auto-applies it
finding.summary: Workflow content is shipped as a committed `git apply`-ready patch, routing the `workflows` permission boundary the trust model rests on through reviewer diligence instead
finding.evidence: The file opens `APPLY WITH: git apply docs/tasks/active/…patch` and explains that it exists because "The agent App … cannot push `.github/workflows/**`". That inability is not an oversight: agent-review-panel.yml:46-52 says the `workflow_run` trigger is chosen "because" of it ("with `checks:write`, the permission the 'check runs are author-unforgeable' property rests on"), and the co-committed lessons file repeats it ("A permission the agent lacks may be the security model, not a gap"). A committed patch whose stated purpose is for a maintainer to apply and push converts a server-enforced boundary into a review-attention question, and it does so in the shape least likely to get workflow-level scrutiny: reviewers see one added `docs/**` file, not a `.github/workflows/**` change, and no lane in this repo lints, type-checks, or executes the blob. The same repo already records this exact anti-pattern as a prior blocking panel finding (scripts/agent/rounds.test.mjs:188-193, on a previous `.patch` under `docs/tasks/active/`), and the lessons file added by this very commit says "A blocked half does not ship as a `.patch` file". This patch's contents happen to be benign (a canary job), which is why it should be raised as a channel rather than as a payload: the next one is reviewed by the same non-mechanism.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims `docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch` is committed and opens with `APPLY WITH: git apply …`. That file does not exist. `Glob **/20260825-promote-exit-code-default*` returns only the `-lessons.md` and `-todo.md` files, and `Glob **/*.patch` returns no files anywhere in the tree (including untracked). A content grep for `APPLY WITH|git apply` yields only Markdown prose, never a patch header or diff blob.

The repository instead documents the withdrawal of exactly this artifact. harness-engineering.md:1988-1999 says the `trigger-shape` canary "is NOT implemented. It was briefly shipped as an apply-ready `.patch` file under `docs/tasks/active/`, and that was withdrawn: routing workflow content past the `workflows` permission boundary as a `git apply` blob makes reviewer diligence the boundary" — and names the mechanical compensating control that did land (`checks.test.mjs` evaluating all three `if:` path clauses against empty, foreign, and real paths). The todo at lines 163-169 states the remaining workflow-file findings "are NOT staged as an apply-ready `.patch` this time" and hands them off as prose for a maintainer. The lessons file at 212-220 is the prohibition itself ("Do not route workflow content through a committed `.patch`"), not evidence of a violation.

The underlying security reasoning (App lacking `workflows` write is load-bearing for the unforgeability of gates 1 and 2, per todo.md:114-131) is correct, but the concrete channel the finding says exists is absent from this working tree, so there is nothing to gate on. Ground: not-present.
groundedIn: docs/tasks/active/ (Glob: no *.patch file exists in repository)

searchedFor: compared pinning/scoping between agent-implement.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and the panel/rerun/loop/ci-report uses
finding.summary: The author/fixer paths mint an UNSCOPED GitHub App installation token from a mutable action tag, which is what makes the gate-2 forgery above reachable
finding.evidence: agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 call `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` with `app-id`/`private-key` and NO `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — handed to a job that then executes model-directed code with the branch checked out. Every other consumer in this repo scopes the token explicitly and pins the action to an immutable SHA for exactly this reason: agent-review-panel.yml:1483-1493 ("Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key", plus `permission-pull-requests: write` / `permission-issues: write`), agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87, ci-report.yml:86-94. Two consequences: (1) if the installation carries `Checks: write`, the unscoped token lets the author agent post its own `agent-review-*` check runs, which `checkPassed` accepts because it never checks `app.slug` — that is the gate-2 bypass reported separately; (2) a compromised or retagged `@v1` reads `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Pre-existing and outside the diff, but the diff's whole premise is that these gates are unforgeable, and the token scope is what decides that.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 both call actions/create-github-app-token@v1 (mutable tag) with only app-id/private-key and NO permission-* inputs, so the minted installation token carries every permission the App installation holds. In both cases that token is handed to actions/checkout of attacker-influenceable branch code (agent-implement.yml:200, with no persist-credentials:false — unlike the trusted sparse checkout at line 62; agent-iterate-ci.yml:115 checking out github.event.workflow_run.head_branch) and exported as GH_TOKEN into the same job that runs the model-directed agent step (agent-implement.yml:395, 455). agent-iterate-ci.yml:117-126 itself states the branch copy is attacker-influenceable code run with a write-carrying token. The repo's own standard is the opposite at every other call site: SHA-pinned d72941d and explicitly scoped (agent-review-panel.yml:1485-1493 and 1800-1808, agent-fix.yml:119-129, agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87, ci-report.yml:86-94), with comments naming this exact risk. In-lane for Security (credential scope / secret exposure / supply chain), and no external guard can constrain an installation token's scope — the permission-* request is the only mechanism and it is absent. One sub-claim is inaccurate: checkPassed DOES filter on app.slug (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:265-272, regression test checks.test.mjs:57-74), so consequence (1) does not hold. That sub-claim is not load-bearing: the unscoped token plus mutable-tag exposure of secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY (agent-implement.yml:122, agent-iterate-ci.yml:109) stands independently, so the finding cannot be refuted.
